correctness.rationale: The nonlinear edge equation is an exact difference of the vertex flow; monotonicity of phi_p proves single-input contraction. At p=2 edge differences satisfy Markov heat; on C3 vertex oscillation equals edge Lipschitz and nonlinear order comparison contracts it. For all n>=4 and p!=2 the explicit zero-sum cyclic edge background and perturbation have a normalized active-edge derivative tending to (p-1)(R^(p-2)-3), unbounded as R tends to infinity (p>2) or zero (1<p<2). Each fixed background has nonzero edges, justifying differentiability even for p<2. Reconstructed exact rational and selected ODE computations corroborate the algebra, not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Complete sharp classification across all cycle sizes and nonlinear exponents, with four vertices the smallest obstruction and arbitrarily large initial normalized edge-gradient sensitivity. This distinguishes single-input smoothing from two-input perturbation stability despite known vertexwise comparison. The cyclic zero-sum constraint produces a genuine topological exception at the triangle and the result is not obtained by reparameterizing earlier tree-only theorems.
